approved: True-up Shortfall Levy (Excise) (Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2013
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that repeals the carbon tax and introduces measures to prevent price exploitation after the repeal.

The package would prohibit businesses from engaging in carbon-specific price exploitation for key goods like electricity and gas, with penalties of up to 6,471 penalty units for corporations and 1,295 penalty units for individuals.
It would also give the ACCC new powers to monitor prices and assess the effect of the carbon tax repeal on certain goods.
Introduces a new prohibition on price exploitation related to the carbon tax repeal for key goods.
Gives the ACCC monitoring powers to assess the effect of the carbon tax repeal on prices.
Introduces a new prohibition on false or misleading representations about the carbon tax repeal's effect on prices.
Businesses and consumers, particularly in markets for key goods such as electricity and gas.

Moved the second reading of a related bill imposing an excise-based true-up shortfall levy to recover the value of overallocated free carbon units issued under the Jobs and Competitiveness Program for the 2013 to 2014 financial year.

Moved a debate management motion to conclude debate on the Clean Energy Legislation (Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2013 and related bills by Thursday this week, arguing the election gave the coalition a mandate with 90 seats to Labor's 55, Labor's worst result since 1903.

Argued against the government's carbon tax repeal bills, saying the decade from 2001 to 2010 was the warmest on record, that Direct Action would cost households an estimated $1,200 a year without a legislated cap on emissions, and noted that under Labor wind power generation trebled and 24,000 renewable energy jobs were created.

The True-up Shortfall Levy (Excise) Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2013 was moved for a second reading. It imposes a levy to recover the value of over-allocated free carbon units under the Jobs and Competitiveness Program for 2013-14, applying only where it is not a duty of customs or excise.
